## Issues by Severity

### Critical

#### C1. Sitemap does not include the canonical-page URLs (only the re-export URLs)
Three real pages exist on the site but are absent from the sitemap; what *is* in the sitemap is the 308-redirected alias:

| Sitemap URL | Real page | 308 alias | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/en/blog` | `/en/resources/blog` (page file exists) | `/en/blog` | `src/app/en/resources/blog/page.tsx` |
| `/en/services/management-system` | `/en/solutions/management-system` (page file exists) | `/en/services/management-system` | `src/app/en/solutions/management-system/page.tsx` |
| `/en/why-us` | `/en/manifesto` (page file exists) | `/en/why-us` | `src/app/en/manifesto/page.tsx` |

All three return 308 Permanent Redirect to the alias in the sitemap. Google will follow the 308 and treat the alias as the canonical, so this is **technically not a duplicate-content risk** — but it is unusual and slightly inefficient. Recommendation: include the canonical-page file paths (`/en/solutions/management-system`, etc.) in the sitemap and **301 the alias to the canonical**, or **remove the alias files entirely** and keep only the canonical (replacing `export { default } from "..."` re-exports with `redirect()` in a `route.ts`).

#### C2. Sitemap hreflang coverage is inconsistent
The sitemap declares `<xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="…">` for:
- ✅ All service pages (`/services/[slug]` × EN/FR)
- ✅ All industry pages (`/industries/[slug]` × EN/FR)
- ✅ All blog category pages (`/blog/category/[slug]` × EN/FR)
- ✅ All blog posts (`/blog/[slug]` × EN/FR)

But **omits** them for the 26 top-level static pages:
- `/en`, `/fr`
- `/en/services`, `/fr/services`
- `/en/case-studies`, `/fr/case-studies`
- `/en/industries`, `/fr/industries`
- `/en/guides`, `/fr/guides`
- `/en/guides/2026-marketing-playbook`, `/fr/guides/2026-marketing-playbook`
- `/en/blog` (index), `/fr/blog` (index)
- `/en/careers`, `/fr/careers`
- `/en/contact`, `/fr/contact`
- `/en/why-us`, `/fr/why-us`
- `/en/privacy`, `/fr/privacy`
- `/en/terms`, `/fr/terms`

**Why this matters:** Google uses hreflang declarations as a **clustering signal** — every page in a language pair should reference every other. Inconsistent signals can cause Google to ignore the cluster for some pages and rank the wrong locale. Recommendation: generate hreflang `<xhtml:link>` for *every* URL that has a translation.

#### C3. Every non-blog `<lastmod>` is the build timestamp
**73 / 76** URLs have `<lastmod>2026-06-07T10:46:48.331Z</lastmod>` — the exact build time captured by `new Date()` inside `sitemap.ts:83`. This is a sitemap-wide *identical* `<lastmod>` and is the exact pattern Google flags in their docs as misleading ("do not fabricate lastmod").

In `src/app/sitemap.ts:83–94, 96–144`, all non-blog entries are emitted with `lastModified: now` (the `Date` object created at the top of the function). The blog entries correctly use `p.datePublished` (`sitemap.ts:147, 156`).

**Why this matters:** Google uses `<lastmod>` to decide whether to re-crawl a page. A "fake" uniform timestamp tells Google every page changes on every build, encouraging unnecessary re-crawls and devaluing the signal. Recommendation: drop `<lastmod>` for static pages that don't have a real modification time, or compute it from `git log -1 --format=%cI` of the page file at build time.

---

### Medium

#### M1. `<priority>` and `<changefreq>` are deprecated by Google
Google announced in **November 2023** that it ignores both `<priority>` and `<changefreq>` in sitemaps. Bing still reads them. They are not harmful, just dead weight. Source: <https://developers.google.com/search/docs/sitemaps/overview> ("Note: Google ignores <priority> and <changefreq> values."). Recommendation: drop both for cleanliness. Optional: keep `<changefreq>` for Bing only.

#### M2. Sitemap is not split by content type
At 76 URLs, splitting is **not required** (the 50,000-URL limit is far from reached). Best-practice splits are `sitemap-pages.xml`, `sitemap-blog.xml`, `sitemap-categories.xml` — but for a site this size, a single `sitemap.xml` is fine. Recommendation: do not split unless URL count exceeds 10,000.

---

### Low / Info

#### I1. Sitemap lastmod for blog posts uses `datePublished`, not `dateModified`
Per `src/app/sitemap.ts:147, 156`:
```ts
lastModified: new Date(p.datePublished),
```
For posts that have been edited since publication, this understates the modification date. The blog loader already exposes `dateModified` (added in the recent schema PR) — recommendation: prefer `p.dateModified ?? p.datePublished` in the sitemap as well, so re-published posts don't lie about their freshness.

#### I2. Robots.txt is healthy
```
User-Agent: *
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Host: https://maroc360.agency
Sitemap: https://maroc360.agency/sitemap.xml
```
Note: `Host:` directive is **ignored by Google** (only Bing reads it), and the `<host>` element in sitemaps is **fully deprecated**. Cosmetic, can be removed. `Disallow: /api/` is fine.

## Related Issues (out of sitemap scope, but found while validating)

### R1. Every page's HTML `<link rel="canonical">` is wrong (CRITICAL — not in sitemap scope)
Source: `src/app/layout.tsx:35–42`

```ts
alternates: {
  canonical: siteConfig.url,        // → "https://maroc360.agency" (root)
  languages: {
    en: siteConfig.url,             // → "https://maroc360.agency"
    fr: `${siteConfig.url}/fr`,     // → "https://maroc360.agency/fr"
    "x-default": siteConfig.url,    // → "https://maroc360.agency"
  },
},
```

This propagates to every page that does not override it. Result:
- Every EN page declares `<link rel="canonical" href="https://maroc360.agency"/>` — pointing every EN page to the homepage.
- Every FR page declares `<link rel="canonical" href="https://maroc360.agency/fr"/>` — pointing every FR page to the FR homepage.

This is a **massive SEO bug** (Google will de-index all inner pages or collapse them onto the homepage). It is pre-existing (not introduced by the recent schema work) but is the single highest-priority SEO fix on the site. Fix: set `alternates.canonical` and `alternates.languages` **per page** in the page-level `metadata` export, or remove the root-level defaults and rely on `metadataBase` + per-page `alternates.canonical: absoluteUrl(path)`.

### R2. HTML `<html lang>` is hardcoded `en`
Every page renders `<html lang="en">` (`src/app/layout.tsx:81`). FR pages should render `<html lang="fr">`. Fix: use a route-group layout for `/fr/*` with its own `<html lang="fr">`, or read the locale from the URL.

### R3. No AI-crawler rules in robots.txt
`Google-Extended`, `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `CCBot` are not explicitly mentioned. By default they are allowed, which is the desired policy for AI citation / GEO. Consider adding a `User-agent: Google-Extended\nDisallow:` block to make the intent explicit. Out of scope for the sitemap audit.

## Recommendations (prioritized)

| # | Action | Severity | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Fix `alternates.canonical` and `alternates.languages` per page** (issue R1) | Critical | M (30 page files) |
| 2 | **Drop `<priority>` and `<changefreq>` from the sitemap** (M1) — or keep for Bing | Medium | XS |
| 3 | **Remove the build-timestamp `<lastmod>` for static pages** (C3) — drop the field entirely for static entries | Medium | XS |
| 4 | **Add hreflang `<xhtml:link>` to all 26 top-level static pages in the sitemap** (C2) | Medium | S |
| 5 | **Switch the blog-post `lastmod` to use `dateModified ?? datePublished`** (I1) | Low | XS |
| 6 | Resolve the re-export vs canonical-page mismatch (C1) — either include the real canonical page in the sitemap and add a `redirect()` from the alias, or delete the alias files | Low | S |
| 7 | Fix `<html lang>` for FR pages (R2) | Critical (i18n) | M |

Items #1 and #7 are out of scope for the sitemap audit and are flagged for the broader SEO tech-audit.
